Absolutely painful Guardians of the Galaxy is a diffuse, unrestrained mess that constantly feels like it is tripping over itself. There are good ideas here, some legitimate emotional material, and a handful of performances and moments that work, but almost none of it is given enough discipline or breathing room to develop real weight. The movie is constantly moving, constantly talking, constantly introducing something new, and constantly trying to be funny. That energy is clearly part of the appeal, but for me it becomes exhausting. The worldbuilding arrives as a flood of names, factions, planets, relationships, and cosmic mythology before much of it has any dramatic meaning. The characters are introduced just as aggressively, but most of them remain surprisingly thin because the movie is always rushing toward the next joke, plot beat, or bit of exposition. That same restlessness hurts the emotional side of the movie. There are real arcs here in theory. Peter is supposed to move from emotional detachment toward connection and sacrifice, Gamora is escaping the control of Thanos and Ronan, Drax is masking grief with rage, Rocket carries the trauma of being experimented on, and Groot ultimately gives himself up for the group. None of those are bad ideas, but most of them feel more stated than fully dramatized. Peter is the clearest example. His arc has a beginning and an end on paper, and the callback to his mother gives it structure, but I never really felt him change all that much. The movie does not establish his emotional detachment strongly enough for his eventual heroism to feel transformative. Gamora has even less to work with because she is already planning to betray Ronan before we really know who she is. Drax is funny, but his grief is largely swallowed by the comedy surrounding him. Rocket and Groot have an emotional bond, but the movie asks for a payoff from a friendship it has mostly treated as comedic side character banter. The humor is probably the biggest reason none of this landed for me. It is not simply that I found most of it unfunny, the problem is that the movie seems almost allergic to sincerity. Whenever something begins to feel tense, emotional, or serious, there is often something to deflate it. It gives the entire movie the feeling of an elbow to the ribs. There are moments where the story finally allows itself to be sincere, and those moments are usually among the strongest in the film, which only makes the constant undercutting more frustrating. That is what ultimately makes the movie feel so sloppy to me. It has potentially interesting mythology, a found family story, trauma, revenge, abuse, sacrifice, and identity all inside it, but very little feels satisfyingly integrated. Ronan is barely more than a generic villain, Nebula isn’t much of a character, the Kree/Xandar conflict mostly exists as exposition, the Infinity Stone material should feel enormous, but even that gets folded into the same hyperactive, ironic tone. There are still things I like. Chris Pratt is charismatic, Dave Bautista gets most of the laughs that worked for me, the movie moves well, some of the imagery is imaginative, and there are a few sincere emotional beats that land when the movie actually allows them to. But those moments feel buried inside a movie whose entire sensibility I found exhausting. Rather than feeling like a refreshing expansion of the MCU, Guardians of the Galaxy feels like a loud, scattered tonal diversion that helped normalize many of the tendencies I would eventually come to dislike most about the franchise. There is enough life, craft, and isolated value here to keep it out of the absolute basement. But I hated watching it.

For every moment of effective film making or character work present, it feels like there are ten other instances of the script being condescending, lazy or inconsistent. The film's humour and visuals are inconsistent. The fight scenes are consistently awful, being permeated with dizzying jump cuts. There are many points where characters just say things that are meant to be funny funny, despite it feeling incongruous with their depiction to that point. The character arcs here are mostly force fed down viewers' throats with any consideration for their gag reflex whatsoever. Peter's actually works pretty well though. I love that his code name isn't based in his pride, but instead a preservation of his mother's love. I enjoy Nebula thoroughly and Rocket is probably the character who got the most chuckles out of me. Nebula staring in awe at Ronin's power and her dejected reaction to Thanos blatantly admitting Gamora is his favourite greatly endears me to her. While this watch isn't totally painful, it certainly leaves me longing for credits to roll. Even the good moments didn't connect for the most part, due to me having seen this film so much. I've become numb to a lot of its charm. Gamora's power-scaling in this film is awful. I still enjoy a handful of scenes a lot.

No terminé Guardianes de la Galaxia porque, siendo sincera, no logré conectar mucho con la historia. Siento que para alguien que ya es fan de Marvel o que está acostumbrado a este tipo de películas de superhéroes puede ser mucho más fácil disfrutarla, pero yo me perdí bastante con la historia y con todos los personajes. Aun así, hay cosas que sí me gustaron muchísimo. El soundtrack me parece increíble y siento que le da una personalidad completamente diferente a la película. También me encantó el estilo de los personajes y cómo cada uno tiene una personalidad tan marcada. Pero lo que más me interesó fue conocer el origen de Peter. La parte de su mamá me pareció muy bonita y triste al mismo tiempo, sobre todo porque la música termina convirtiéndose en algo muy importante para él, como una forma de mantener cerca esos recuerdos y sentirse conectado con ella. Siento que esa parte fue lo que más me hizo conectar con la película. En general, entiendo por qué a tanta gente le encanta, porque tiene personajes muy diferentes, un estilo propio y un soundtrack buenísimo, pero personalmente sentí que no estaba entendiendo del todo lo que estaba pasando y por eso no pude disfrutarla como esperaba.

Guardians of the Galaxy funciona principalmente pela personalidade que James Gunn consegue dar a personagens que, isoladamente, poderiam ser pouco interessantes. Peter Quill, Gamora, Rocket, Groot e Drax começam como figuras incompatíveis e passam boa parte do filme discutindo, competindo e tentando sobreviver uns aos outros. É justamente nessa convivência que o filme encontra seus melhores momentos. A trilha escolhida por Quill também dá uma identidade própria ao universo cósmico e cria um contraste divertido com toda aquela grandiosidade espacial. O problema é que a história ao redor do grupo é muito mais convencional. Ronan é um antagonista pouco interessante, a Joia do Infinito funciona como mais um objeto capaz de destruir mundos e o terceiro ato retorna ao espetáculo previsível do gênero. O humor também nem sempre funciona para mim. Ainda assim, existe uma química genuína entre os protagonistas que sustenta boa parte da experiência. Guardians of the Galaxy me interessa pouco como aventura cósmica, mas funciona bem melhor como história sobre cinco pessoas improváveis aprendendo a permanecer juntas.
